question: Can numerical geometric data lead to simpler models?
idea: One claim says that, under the stated positivity conditions, a canonical class with an extra nonnegative part has the same numerical behavior as a class defining a map. A separate claim supplies minimal models or fiber-space models for specified generalized pairs. Numerical equivalence is weaker than equality of classes.
why: The study of shapes defined by equations, often using complex numbers. It connects geometric features with algebraic rules.

A kind of geometric space in which complex coordinates, lengths, and an additional geometric structure are compatible.
A mathematical condition that rules out certain forms of escaping to infinity; in ordinary Euclidean space it means closed and bounded.

exactClaim: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints $K_X+B+M$ with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case. Separately, projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed.
